children: Suchi Semicon has started commercial production at its semiconductor packaging facility in Gujarat and plans to scale capacity tenfold to 3 million chips a day within three years, as global semiconductor companies increasingly approach the Indian OSAT player for packaging and testing, its Chairman, Ashok Mehta said on Thursday.
The company currently has a production capacity of 3,00,000 chips a day and has customers lined up for the planned expansion, Mehta said on the sidelines of Semicon India 2026.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday virtually inaugurated the company’s OSAT facility in Surat, marking the commencement of commercial production. The facility is among the first OSAT projects approved under the India Semiconductor Mission to move from project approval to commercial operations.
Modi noted that 12 semiconductor projects have been approved so far under the India Semiconductor Mission and that the next phase would expand the country’s chipmaking ecosystem.
“We have demand from customers for 3 million chips a day. We just have to build the capacity and deliver to them,” Mehta said.

The approved project has an investment of $100 million. Suchi Semicon received Cabinet approval for its OSAT project under the India Semiconductor Mission in May 2026, with ₹868 crore in approved support.

The semiconductor OSAT company provides packaging and testing solutions for automotive, industrial, consumer electronics, power electronics and EV applications. Its Surat packaging facility has capabilities spanning SOIC, QFN and power semiconductor packaging.

Since its incorporation in 2023, the company has commissioned its Class 10K and 100K cleanrooms, completed its first customer shipment, and established a technology collaboration with Japan’s ROHM Semiconductor.

Mehta said sample production for customer qualification following the ROHM collaboration had triggered interest from several global semiconductor companies, changing perceptions about India’s ability to handle semiconductor packaging.
“Three years ago, when we started, people were wondering if India could pull this off. Today, they are simply approaching us for packaging and qualification.”

Mehta said most of the company’s current customer interest was from global semiconductor companies, across the United States, Japan, Korea and Europe. Working with Indian fabless companies can involve Suchi managing the wafers and packaging and delivery, making it a more complex proposition, he said.
For now, Suchi is focused on qualifying products and increasing capacity rather than near-term revenue and profitability. Customer qualification can take six months to a year, he said.

The company plans to move into advanced packaging in its next phase, while continuing to expand its existing operations. Over the next three years, Suchi Semicon also aims to scale production capacity to one billion chips per year and create more than 600 direct jobs at the Surat facility.

title: Suchi Semicon starts commercial production, targets 3 million chips a day over three years
